newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL STOCK EXCHANGE CHIEF BLAMES RINGGIT WEAKNESS.
newsitem.headline: KL STOCK EXCHANGE CHIEF BLAMES RINGGIT WEAKNESS.

text.p: The fall in Malaysian share prices was due to a decline of the ringgit against the U.S. dollar, Nik Mohamad Din Nik Yusoff, executive chairman of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Tuesday.

"From what I can see it is the weakening of the ringgit. That seems to be the factor causing the market to weaken," he told reporters after launching the Jardine Fleming Apex Malaysia Growth Trust fund.
"There is nothing wrong with the economy. The fundamentals are good," Nik Din said.
"That is why I urge people to go into the market to buy now. There is nothing adverse about our economy," he said.
The KLSE's key blue-chip index has been falling sharply in the last few weeks, hitting a new 21-month low on Tuesday morning.
A few minutes after the lunch break on Tuesday, the Composite Index was at 887.05 points, down 15.09 or 1.67 percent.
